id.description: A screen name of the vocabulary: one or two kebab-case segments.

title.description: The title of the screen, for a reader.

description.description: What the screen is for: the task it serves and when it is shown. Not a list of its parts: each anchor has its own description. See the rule `description-purposes`. At most 200 characters.

frame.description: The frame around every screen: it has no route of its own.

path.description: The route path: static segments, `$param`, `{-$param}` (optional) and `$` (splat), from `/`.

guard.description: Where an account the route is not for is sent: a guest to sign-in (`authenticated`), or a signed-in account to the profile (`guest`); absent: nobody is sent.

roles.description: The roles the route serves: it opens for an account that holds one, after the guard and before the search is read, and the not-found screen opens at the same address for any other.

params.description: The path parameters, as a flat JSON Schema.

type.description: The primitive type of the parameter.

items.description: A string, number or boolean value.

default.description: The value when the URL leaves it out.

examples.description: Fake values of the parameter, each one it accepts; the first fills the example link.

items.description: A string, number or boolean value.

minimum.description: The smallest value of a number or an integer.

maximum.description: The largest value of a number or an integer.

minLength.description: The fewest characters of a string.

maxLength.description: The most characters of a string.

pattern.description: A regular expression (ECMA-262) every value of a string matches.

description.description: What the route parameter means. Its type, bounds, default and examples say the rest. At most 200 characters.

control.description: The anchor of the control that sets the parameter.

values.description: Per enum value, the control that chooses it.

control.description: The anchor of the control that chooses this value.

controlValue.description: The data-value of that control which chooses this value.

note.description: Anything a reader needs to know about the value.

additionalProperties.description: How a page sets one enum value of the parameter.

x-perch.description: The controls of the page that set the parameter.

additionalProperties.description: One flat parameter.
Always false: no other parameter.

key.description: Makes the parameter the screen's key: a value of it missing or broken is the failure with this code, one of an action the screen runs with `{ search: <name> }` whose parameter refers to a value. A route has one key, and a key has no `default`. See the rule `address-key`.

x-perch.description: The controls of the page that set the parameter, and whether it is the screen's key.

additionalProperties.description: One flat parameter.
Always false: no other parameter.

history.description: Whether opening the route adds a history entry or replaces the current one.

retain.description: The search parameters carried across navigations.

bindings.description: The routes of the screen: at least one unless the screen is the frame.

flag.description: The feature flag that shows the screen, or null for always.

entry.description: The anchors that are present once the screen is open.

propertyNames.description: A declared anchor: 2 to 4 dot-separated kebab-case segments, kind last.

kind.description: The kind of the anchor; matches the end of its last segment.

description.description: What the element is for. Its kind, binding, codes, states, roles and flow say the rest; leave out what the engine says itself. See the rule `description-purposes`. At most 200 characters.

items.description: What the anchor is bound to: a model field, an action, a route, or the search parameter a field starts with.

anyOf.description: Several bindings: the anchor runs them in this order, or one of them depending on the mode of the screen; the flow says which.

binding.description: What the anchor does or shows: a field of the model, an action, a route, or (on a field that holds no secret) the search parameter it starts with. See the rules `anchor-binding` and `flow-effects`.

roles.description: Who sees the element, among the roles its screen's bindings serve. Absent, it adds no limit: those above it and a link's derived roles hold. See the rules `anchor-roles`, `roles` and `link-roles`.

own.description: Shown to a member only on the entries the member owns: the anchor sits in an entry of a list, and shows on the entries the member owns alone. See the rule `own-entries`.

holdsInput.description: Whether typed text stays in the field until an action takes it or a `clear` empties it. Left out, it is derived: false where its own change alone applies it at once. See the rule `field-holds-input`.

marksState.description: `false`: an `input`, `textarea` or `select` that holds input shows no state colour, its `data-state` still kept. Left out, it shows it. See the rules `state-colour` and `check-sources`.

secret.description: A field that holds a secret (a password, its confirmation, a current password): it never comes from or goes into a URL, and leaves only in its action's request. See the rule `secret-field`.

anyOf.description: A declared anchor: 2 to 4 dot-separated kebab-case segments, kind last.

propertyNames.description: A declared anchor: 2 to 4 dot-separated kebab-case segments, kind last.

anyOf.description: The anchor, with the codes it shows meanwhile.

items.description: An anchor of the screen, or `{ <anchor>: [codes] }`: that anchor while it shows one of these codes.

with.description: The element renders only while every entry matches: an anchor while it renders, `{ <anchor>: [codes] }` while that anchor shows one of the codes. See the rule `with-without`.

anyOf.description: A declared anchor: 2 to 4 dot-separated kebab-case segments, kind last.

without.description: The element renders only while no entry matches: an anchor while it renders, `{ <anchor>: [codes] }` while that anchor shows one of the codes. See the rule `with-without`.

codes.description: `data-code` values on a `message`, `error`, `toast` or `dialog`: vocabulary or derived toast codes; tests assert them, not words. An error may leave them out. See the rule `error-codes-and-fields`.

ranked.description: A message whose codes are in rank order: of the codes raised before it shows, it shows the first. Only on a message of two codes or more, each listed once. See the rule `ranked-message`.

fields.description: Each error code with its field or `form`. From version 3 written entries override the derived code by code; before, they replace them all. See the rules `error-codes-and-fields` and `error-placement`.

anyOf.description: A declared anchor: 2 to 4 dot-separated kebab-case segments, kind last.

additionalProperties.description: A field of the screen, by its anchor, or `form`, the form as a whole.

dataId.description: What the `data-id` of the element holds: the id of the entity it shows, on an `item` or a `row`. A `data-id` is data, not contract: no check reads its value. See the rule `attributes`.

dataValue.description: It or its options carry a `data-value`, a choice's stable key, not its label. From version 4 the loader sets it on a select; a screen file omits it there. See the rules `attributes` and `kind-parts`.

states.description: The `data-state` values it takes: an app, container or row state. Not the field states of an `input`, `textarea` or `select`: `ids` lists those. See the rules `attributes` and `field-states-carried`.

derived.description: The derived suffixes it renders; a screen file omits a paged list's parts and, from version 4, a kind's own: the loader lists them. See the rules `derived-parts`, `kind-parts` and `visibility-button`.

entity.description: The entity of model.schema.json the anchor lists.

order.description: The field the entries are ordered by.

anyOf.description: The entries come from an entity of the model: the anchor follows the stored data as it changes, here or on another device, and is never read.

platform.description: The platform action whose result the anchor lists.

value.description: The constant: a string, a number or a boolean.

anyOf.description: A constant the parameter always takes: `{ "value": true }`.

search.description: The name of a search parameter every route of the screen declares.

anyOf.description: The value of a search parameter of the route the screen was opened at: `{ "search": "token" }`, the token a link carries.

params.description: Per parameter of the action, a search parameter of the route `{ "search": "<name>" }`, which the list reads again when it becomes another, or a constant; never a field. See the rule `list-reads`.

paged.description: The list is a page of the action's entries: its page and size are the route's search parameters, and its parts are derived, never written. See the rule `paged-list`.

anyOf.description: The entries come from a platform action, which the anchor reads when it starts to render, when what it reads for changes, and where a flow says `read: <anchor>`. See the rule `list-reads`.

source.description: Where a list's, section's or table's entries come from, and when they are read; no other kind has one. See the rule `list-reads` for when a list reads and the rule `paged-list` for a paged one.

composite.description: The platform composite the field opts into, declared once in `platform.yaml`; the loader derives its list and items. Only a secret `input` opts in. See the rule `composite-of-the-platform`.

confirms.description: Written on an unbound secret input: names the other secret input of its screen, one that opts into a composite, whose password it repeats. See the rule `password-pair`.

confirm.description: `false`: no question before its destructive action. Left out, a control bound to one asks if the frame has a confirmation; refused on others. See the rule `destructive-question`.

additionalProperties.description: One declared anchor, as a screen file writes it.

states.description: The container states of the screen, rows of the vocabulary's Container states table: what is visible in each, never what each means. See the rule `readiness`.

additionalProperties.description: What is visible on the screen in this container state; the vocabulary says what the state means, and each anchor what it is for in a description of its own. At most 200 characters.

id.description: The id of the machine: one segment, which the app gives its machine and an id target `#<id>.<state>` names; absent, the screen id. See the rule `flow-states`.

description.description: What the flow does as a whole that no single state says: how its areas or its modes go together. Its states, events, guards and effects say the rest. At most 200 characters.

initial.description: The state the screen opens in.

meta.description: What the contract says of the flow beyond XState: its guards and the sets of anchors its states render.

guards.description: The guards by name, each with what it holds.

propertyNames.description: A guard: a camelCase name of the flow `meta.guards`.

anyOf.description: What the guard holds, in one sentence the app implements; a guard that tells the failures of an action apart takes their codes, `{ codes }`, instead. At most 200 characters.

codes.description: The codes it holds for: the action failed with one of them.

anyOf.description: A guard by failure code, on a branch of an `onError` only: it holds when the action failed with one of its codes.

additionalProperties.description: What a guard holds: a sentence, or the failure codes it holds for.

target.description: The state the machine moves to; absent: it stays where it is.

guard.description: A guard: a camelCase name of the flow `meta.guards`.

read.description: Only where this outcome changes no list: nothing reads after it. On an invoke's `onDone` or `onError` branch, never beside a `read` or under `read: false`. See the rule `read-after-an-action`.

description.description: What follows that the target, the guard and the effects do not say: where a success leads, what a failure shows, what restarts what. At most 200 characters.

anyOf.description: One transition.

authoredTransition.description: One transition, in full or as its target alone.
